newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- New Aspiration Party leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's long-cherished dream came true when he was officially appointed Thailand's 22nd prime minister yesterday. Speculation continues over his cabinet which is still being worked out. Coalition leaders plan to meet again today to finalise the cabinet list so Chavalit can submit it to the King tomorrow. The Cabinet members will probably be sworn in on December 1. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Thailand will today use an aide memoire to ensure visiting U.S. President Bill Clinton receives the full message from Thailand on what it expects from the United States as well as the Kingdom's response to U.S. demands in their bilateral relations. A 40-minute discussion between Clinton and outgoing Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa, will cover a wide range of issues ranging from economic, security, to human rights, as well as Thailand's wish to cooperate with transnational U.S. problems concerning such things as drug trafficking and money laundering. (THE NATION)

- The Police Department has taken the first steps towards establishing a new division responsible for the fight against computer hackers and to tackle computer-related crime. The new division will be a step toward enabling police with enough know-how to fight the crimes. (THE NATION)

- The state-run National Housing Authority has outlined measures to assist developers suffering from the prolonged slowdown in the real estate business. The measures include an investment of more than 10 billion baht to buy 20,000 housing units of which developers were unable to sell earlier. (MANAGER)

- A double-taxation treaty between Thailand and the United States, to be signed during President Bill Clinton's visit today, will greatly help attract American fund managers to the Thai equity market. American investors are now taxed in both countries at 10 percent on capital gains and 15 percent on dividends from their investments in Thai equities. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) will commence its privatisation programme by spinning off three main units into corporations early next year before seeking stock market listings for them in late 1998. PTT will spin-off PTT Oil, PTT International and PTT Gas into separate business entities in early 1997. (THE NATION)
